key_insight: The paper uses machine learning to search for effective link simplifications, producing new upper bounds and many exact values for hard-to-compute invariants such as slice genus, unknotting number, and strong slice genus.
engineering_relevance: It shows how reinforcement learning and Bayesian optimization can guide combinatorial search in topology when exact algorithms are unavailable, yielding practical bound estimates and discovered transformation trajectories.
method: Reinforcement learning to find unknotting or slice-genera-improving moves for links
Bayesian optimization to improve upper bounds on link invariants
Combine learned upper bounds with known lower bounds to certify exact values when they meet
evidence_signal: The abstract reports new upper bounds, many newly exact values, and recovered non-additivity counterexamples for the unknotting number, including new unknotting trajectories in some cases.
watch_item: The approach provides bounds and certificates via comparison with known invariants, but it does not make these link invariants algorithmically computable in general.
paper_title: Computations of the slice genus and the unknotting number of links via machine learning
